title: कालिकोटे भाषिका र मानक नेपाली भाषाका काल र पक्षको व्यतिरेकी अध्ययन
nepali: भाषा भत्राले भावाभिव्यञ्जन गर्ने माध्यमलाई बुझिन्छ । भाषाको मुख्य प्रयोग ध्वनिसङ्केतहरूको सहायताबाट भावको अभिव्यञ्जनका लागि हुन्छ । ध्वनि सङ्केतबाट मात्र भनाइको पूर्णता र स्पष्टता हुन सक्छ । भाषा शब्द संस्कृतको भाष् धातुबाट निष्पत्र भएको हो जसको अर्थ व्यक्तिवाणी हुन्छ । भाषाको कथ्यरूप नै मूल रूप हो । प्रत्येक भाषामा आफ्नै खाले शब्दभण्डार अर्थव्यवस्था र व्याकरणिक व्यवस्था हन्ु छ । समयको अन्तराल, भौगोलिक विकटता, सांस्कृतिक तथा राजनीतिक विविधता र बसाइँ सराइका कारणले भाषिक रूपमा विविधता आउँछ । तत्पश्चात् एउटै भाषाभित्र विभित्र भाषिकाहरूको प्रादुर्भाव हन्ु छ । यिनै भाषिकाहरूको समुच्चय नै भाषा हो भाषाको प्राचीनता र भौगोलिक दूरता जति बढ्यो त्यति नै बढी भाषिकाहरू जन्मने सम्भावना रहन्छ । समाजका सदस्यहरू आपसमा सञ्चार विनिमय गर्दा भाषिकाको नै प्रयोग गर्दछन् । भाषा प्रायः औपचारिक, स्तरीय र स्थिर प्रकृतिको हुन्छ भने भाषिका अनौपचारिक, स्वतःस्फूर्त र गतिशील हुन्छ । स्थानअनुसार भाषाका व्यवस्थामा सामान्य भित्रता पैदा हुन्छ । कुनै खास स्थानमा बसोबास गर्ने व्यक्तिहरूले बोल्ने भाषाको क्षेत्रीय रूप नै भाषिका हो । एउटै भाषिका बोल्ने व्यक्तिहरूको भाषाका उच्चारण, रूप, शब्दभण्डार, वाक्यगठन, अर्थ, व्याकरणिक कोटिहरूजस्ता समग्र व्यवस्थामा पूर्णतया समानता हुन्छ । यिनै आधारमा रही यहाँ कालिकोटे भाषिका र मानक नेपाली भाषाबिच काल र पक्षबिच तुलनात्मक अध्ययन गरिएको छ । कालिकोट जिल्लाका कोटबाडा, कुमालगाउँ, रकु, सिउना र नानीकोट गााविसहरूलाई प्रमुख अध्ययन क्षेत्र मानी क्षेत्रीय अध्ययन विधिको आधारमा व्यतिरेकी अध्ययन गरिएको छ । यस क्रममा अन्तवार्ता, छलफल र प्रश्नोत्तर गरी सामग्री सङ्कलन गरी प्राप्त सामग्रीलाई सत्यापन गरिएको छ । प्राप्त सामग्रीलाई शोध अध्ययन विधि र पुस्तकालयीय अध्ययन विधि प्रयोग गरी निष्कर्षमा पुग्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Language is understood to mean the medium that expresses emotion. The main use of language is to express emotion through sound symbols. Only through sound symbols can the completeness and clarity of an utterance be achieved. The word 'bhāṣā' is derived from the Sanskrit root 'bhāṣ', whose meaning is individual speech. The spoken form of language is the original form. Every language has its own vocabulary, semantic arrangement, and grammatical arrangement. Because of the passage of time, geographical remoteness, cultural and political diversity, and migration, diversity arises in linguistic form. After that, various dialects emerge within the same language. These dialects taken together constitute language; the greater the language's antiquity and geographical distance increase, the more the likelihood of more dialects being born remains. When members of society exchange communication among themselves, they use the dialect itself. Language is generally formal, stratified, and static in nature, whereas dialect is informal, spontaneous, and dynamic. According to location, ordinary differences arise within the arrangements of a language. The regional form of the language spoken by people living in a particular place is the dialect. In the overall arrangement of the language of people speaking the same dialect, such as pronunciation, form, vocabulary, sentence construction, meaning, and grammatical categories, there is complete similarity. On this very basis, a comparative study of tense and aspect between the Kalikote dialect and standard Nepali has been carried out here. Considering the Kotbada, Kumalgaun, Raku, Siuna, and Nanikot village development committees of Kalikot district as the main study areas, a contrastive study was conducted on the basis of the field-study method. In this process, material was collected through interviews, discussions, and question-and-answer sessions, and the material obtained was verified. An attempt was made to reach conclusions by using the research-study method and the library-study method with the material obtained.

Over stretches of time, with geographical ruggedness, cultural and political diversity, and people shifting around, linguistic diversity turns up. Then different dialects spring up inside the one language. Put those dialects together and you have the language; the older a language gets and the wider the gaps between places, the better the odds of fresh dialects turning up. On that very basis, a comparison of tense and aspect between the Kalikote dialect and standard Nepali has been done here. Taking the Kotbada, Kumalgaun, Raku, Siuna, and Nanikot VDCs of Kalikot district as the main study areas, a contrastive study was done using the field-study method. Along the way, material was collected through interviews, discussions, and Q&A, and what was collected was checked. An effort was made to get to conclusions by running the material collected through the research-study method and the library-study method.
